subject: Discovery Recap: AcmeHealth Private VPC Requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery Recap: AcmeHealth Private VPC Requirements

Hi Alex — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have alignment. Please let me know if I missed anything or if any of the priorities below should be reprioritized.

Summary of pain points and goals
- Regulated PHI workloads: must run in a customer-managed VPC with no egress to public model endpoints.
- KMS / keys: require customer-managed keys (CMK) / HSM integration for model encryption at rest.
- Network constraints: strict firewall rules, only specific outbound ports allowed, and traffic must traverse their VNet; potential need for a private link or private endpoint.
- Air-gap / on-prem consideration: evaluated if a packaged on-prem appliance is required for isolated sites.
- Audit & compliance: SOC 2 evidence, audit logs, and retention policy required for all inference requests.
- Latency & throughput targets: sub-200ms p95 for typical inference paths; pilot must demonstrate predictable latency under 100 qps.

Current stack (what you shared)
- Primary EHR cluster in Azure (VNet) with Azure AD for identity.
- Customer currently encrypts sensitive data with Azure Key Vault (HSM-backed).
- Splunk for logging, and internal SIEM ingest requirements.

Success criteria for initial pilot
1) Private VPC deployment inside AcmeHealth VNet (no public internet egress).
2) Customer-managed key integration for model artifacts and logs.
3) Evidence pack (SOC 2 summary, network ports, and audit log samples) delivered before pilot kickoff.
4) Pilot demonstrating <200ms p95 latencies at target throughput and autoscaling behavior.

Immediate next steps
- I will share our standard Private/VPC checklist and a network port list (attached: network-requirements.xlsx).
- Provide SOC 2 summary and architecture diagram (attached: private-vpc-architecture-diagram.pdf).
- Schedule a 60-min technical deep dive with your infra + security team to validate network and key management details — suggested times next week.
- Share an initial statement of work and pilot SOW for procurement and legal review.

Action owners
- Marissa: send security pack & network reqs (attached) — by EOD today.
- Alex: confirm any additional non-standard firewall rules and add procurement + CTO to thread.
- Dylan / Aditya: prepare pilot sizing and confirm on-call engineering for the deep dive.

Thanks again — excited to help AcmeHealth get a secure Private deployment running.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: network-requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet), private-vpc-architecture-diagram.pdf (diagram)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Sara Lee <sara.lee@acmehealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 17:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: AcmeHealth Private VPC Requirements

Marissa — thanks for the thorough recap. Confirming the list looks complete from our side. A few clarifications and notes: 

- We absolutely need CMK/HSM integration for encryption of model artifacts and any persisted caches. Azure Key Vault is our standard (HSM-backed).
- For egress: we cannot allow any outbound connections to public IPs. We expect Redwood to support private endpoints or a direct peering model.
- Audit logs: retention 7 years for certain event types; we'll send a sanitized sample set and our retention policy to help scope storage.

Procurement (cc'd) — please put us on your internal calendar for next steps on the SOW and contracts; we expect standard BAAs and the possibility of a longer security review.

Sara — FYI on the latency/throughput expectations — if we can hit the pilot SLOs, we can move forward with a 6-month pilot.

Next steps
- I'll follow up with the sanitized audit log sample by Tue.
- Procurement: please review the SOW once Marissa shares the draft.
- Scheduling: we can do Tuesday 11/17 10:00am PT or Wednesday 11/18 2:00pm PT for the technical deep dive.

Thanks — Alex
